text: Write a function 'filterEvens' that takes an array of integers and returns a new array containing only the even numbers. If there are no even numbers, return an empty array.
Write a function 'findMax' that takes an array of integers and returns the largest number. If the array is empty, return null.
Write a function 'addTwo' that takes two numbers and returns their sum.
Write a function 'isEven' that takes a number and returns true if it is even, false otherwise.
Write a function 'reverseString' that takes a string and returns it reversed.
Write a function 'arrayLength' that takes an array and returns its length.
Write a function 'greet' that takes a name (string) and returns 'Hello, {name}!'.
Write a function 'square' that takes a number and returns its square.
Write a function 'firstElement' that takes an array and returns its first element. If the array is empty, return null.
Write a function 'lastElement' that takes an array and returns its last element. If the array is empty, return null.
Write a function 'sumArray' that takes an array of numbers and returns their sum. Return 0 for an empty array.
Write a function 'toUpperCase' that takes a string and returns it in uppercase.
Write a function 'isPositive' that takes a number and returns true if it is positive (greater than 0), false otherwise.
Write a function 'multiply' that takes two numbers and returns their product.
Write a function 'countVowels' that takes a string and returns the number of vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in it (case-insensitive).
Write a function 'removeFirst' that takes an array and returns a new array with the first element removed. Return empty array if input is empty.
Write a function 'isPalindrome' that takes a string and returns true if it reads the same forwards and backwards, false otherwise (case-sensitive).
Write a function 'absolute' that takes a number and returns its absolute value.
Write a function 'repeatString' that takes a string and a number n, and returns the string repeated n times.
Write a function 'minOfTwo' that takes two numbers and returns the smaller one.
Write a function 'containsValue' that takes an array and a value, and returns true if the array contains the value, false otherwise.
Write a function 'countOccurrences' that takes an array and a value, and returns how many times the value appears in the array.
Write a function 'isString' that takes a value and returns true if it is of type string, false otherwise.
Write a function 'numberToString' that takes a number and returns it as a string.
Write a function 'getKeys' that takes an object and returns an array of its keys.
Write a function 'getValues' that takes an object and returns an array of its values.
Write a function 'concatenateArrays' that takes two arrays and returns a new array that is the concatenation of both.
Write a function 'trimString' that takes a string and returns it with leading and trailing whitespace removed.
Write a function 'maxOfTwo' that takes two numbers and returns the larger one.
Write a function 'filterOdds' that takes an array of integers and returns a new array containing only the odd numbers.
Write a function 'stringLength' that takes a string and returns its length.
Write a function 'power' that takes a base and an exponent and returns base raised to the power of exponent.
Write a function 'splitString' that takes a string and a delimiter, and returns an array of substrings split by the delimiter.
Write a function 'joinArray' that takes an array of strings and a separator, and returns a single string joined by the separator.
Write a function 'isArray' that takes a value and returns true if it is an array, false otherwise.
Write a function 'clampNumber' that takes a number, a min, and a max value, and returns the number clamped within [min, max].
Write a function 'removeLastElement' that takes an array and returns a new array with the last element removed. Return empty array if input is empty.
Write a function 'startsWithCapital' that takes a string and returns true if the first character is an uppercase letter, false otherwise.
Write a function 'objectHasKey' that takes an object and a key string, and returns true if the object has that key, false otherwise.
Write a function 'sortAscending' that takes an array of numbers and returns a new array sorted in ascending order.
Write a function 'capitalize' that takes a string and returns it with the first character converted to uppercase.
Write a function 'subtractTwo' that takes two numbers a and b and returns a minus b.
Write a function 'groupByParity' that takes an array of integers and returns an object with two keys: 'even' (array of even numbers) and 'odd' (array of odd numbers).
Write a function 'uniqueValues' that takes an array and returns a new array with duplicate values removed, preserving the original order.
Write a function 'flattenOnce' that takes a nested array (one level deep) and returns a single flattened array.
Write a function 'wordFrequency' that takes a string of space-separated words and returns an object mapping each word to its count.
Write a function 'chunkArray' that takes an array and a chunk size n, and returns a new array of arrays each of length n (the last chunk may be smaller).
Write a function 'zipArrays' that takes two arrays and returns a new array of pairs [a, b] where each pair contains elements at the same index. Stop at the shorter array's length.
Write a function 'deepEqual' that takes two values and returns true if they are deeply equal (same structure and values for objects/arrays), false otherwise.
Write a function 'sortByProperty' that takes an array of objects and a property name, and returns the array sorted in ascending order by that property's value.
Write a function 'invertObject' that takes an object and returns a new object where the keys and values are swapped.
Write a function 'fibonacci' that takes a number n and returns the nth Fibonacci number (0-indexed, where fib(0) = 0, fib(1) = 1).
Write a function 'mergeObjects' that takes two objects and returns a new object with all key-value pairs from both (second object's values overwrite the first on conflict).
Write a function 'longestWord' that takes a sentence (string) and returns the longest word. If there are ties, return the first one.
Write a function 'rotateArray' that takes an array and a number k, and returns a new array rotated to the right by k positions.
Write a function 'countWords' that takes a string and returns the number of words in it. Words are separated by spaces.
Write a function 'intersection' that takes two arrays and returns a new array of elements that appear in both (no duplicates).
Write a function 'differenceArray' that takes two arrays and returns elements that are in the first array but NOT in the second.
Write a function 'factorial' that takes a non-negative integer n and returns n! (n factorial). Return 1 for n = 0.
Write a function 'mapValues' that takes an object and a function, and returns a new object with the same keys but values transformed by the function.
Write a function 'anagramCheck' that takes two strings and returns true if they are anagrams of each other (same characters, different order, case-insensitive), false otherwise.
Write a function 'binarySearch' that takes a sorted array of numbers and a target, and returns the index of the target, or -1 if not found.
Write a function 'deepFlatten' that takes a deeply nested array and returns a completely flattened array.
Write a function 'memoize' that takes a function and returns a memoized version that caches results for repeated calls with the same arguments (assume single-argument functions).

text: Write a function 'debounce' that takes a function fn and a delay in ms, and returns a debounced version that only calls fn after delay ms have passed since the last invocation.

test_cases.input: debounce called multiple times within delay
debounce called twice with gap > delay

text: Write a function 'longestIncreasingSubsequence' that takes an array of integers and returns the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
Write a function 'curry' that takes a function of arity n and returns a curried version that can be called one argument at a time until all arguments are provided, then returns the result.
Write a function 'groupBy' that takes an array and a key function, and returns an object grouping array items by the key returned by the function for each item.
Write a function 'permutations' that takes an array and returns all possible permutations as an array of arrays.
Write a function 'pipe' that takes any number of functions as arguments and returns a new function that applies them left-to-right (output of each becomes input of the next).
Write a function 'topKFrequent' that takes an array of integers and a number k, and returns the k most frequently occurring elements (in any order).
